summary.intent: Harden the Callisto Rust project: audit CI and test coverage gaps, then start closing them (CI checks for unused deps and semver, blocking per-crate coverage, meaningful edge-case tests), and later refresh docs (readme, arch, contributing, doc generation). The user also asked to confirm published binaries include all features.
summary.outcome: Removed two unused deps from callisto-manifests (found by machete), added edge-case and error-state tests for cargo and npm manifests (coverage 89.22% to 90.69%), updated the justfile and callisto-ci.yml to add checks and make per-crate coverage blocking, and ran full CI before committing and opening a PR. Property tests for the cascade, other test gaps, lint hardening, scheduled mutants/fuzz jobs and docs updates remain.

repo: Invariant 6: shipped crates have no Cargo features, so published binaries can't omit features; a recipe checks the features boundary and that the shipped binary does not enable test-util.
CI runs just recipes; local `just` recipes exist for machete, semver-checks, mutants, fuzz, check-api and coverage-per-crate, but only some were wired into CI.
Per-crate coverage was previously warn-only; callisto-manifests was the one crate under the 90% target.
Test files are split per module (e.g. crates/callisto-manifests/src/cargo/tests.rs, npm/tests.rs) with existing helpers to reuse.
The workspace has edition 2024, MSRV 1.96, unsafe_code forbidden, unwrap_used denied in lib/bin code, cargo-deny, nextest and a 90% overall coverage gate.
Windows is documented as unsupported in stability.md.
Seven proptest suites exist, none for version cascading.

code.finding: `is_publishable` and `bin_names` decide what gets published and which binaries ship, and were under-tested (publish variants, workspace version parse failures, unsupported-operation error).
Had uncovered regions that were closed with new edge-case tests in npm/tests.rs.

workflow: Close coverage gaps with real tests instead of lowering the gate, and verify the gate passes locally before making it blocking.
Verify tool findings (e.g. machete) with a grep and a full rebuild before removing dependencies, and check that the lockfile diff only contains the expected edges.
Use small throwaway scripts (lowcov.py, uncovered.py) to turn coverage data into lists of least-covered files and uncovered line ranges.
Run actionlint and workflow contract checks plus full CI locally before opening the PR.

friction: Every Release workflow run since the previous night failed because the verify job lacked the workflow linters; PR #368 was opened to fix it and must merge first.
Several Bash invocations had to be repeated or split (machete output, workflow lint, remove-deps command), suggesting tool output or command-chaining hiccups.
Per-crate coverage for callisto-manifests was 21 lines short, which blocked making the gate enforce.
open_items: Property tests for cascade.rs (71% coverage): dependency ranges stay consistent and fixed-group versions stay equal.
Tests for release/capability.rs staleness and trust checks, CLI release.rs execute path (receipts, partial failures, reruns) and add.rs.
Edge-case tests for registry.rs, binding.rs and release_decision.rs.
Lint hardening on library crates (dbg_macro, todo, unimplemented, print_stdout), applied crate by crate.
Weekly scheduled cargo-mutants and short fuzz-run jobs on the manifest parsers.
Decide whether the v1 promise should include Windows support.
Verify that artifact attestations cover the CLI binaries and consider an SBOM.
Update the readme, architecture doc, contributing guide and doc generation, as the user requested.
